evidence.caveat: Snapshot is not a proof that new AI technology will improve sales or user value.

root_cause: Existing autonomous daily probe explicitly has null production fitness/challenger values and writes only a read-only contract snapshot. Existing revenue and portal compound dashboard provides source evidence but not a deterministic technology innovation agenda that original owners can consume and implement through protected release.
correction: Add bounded six-lane technology innovation planning to existing owner-only compound proof, using original source-grounded CRO, sales, learning, runtime and customer portal data. Expose ranked source-grounded technology experiments, failure classes, original owners, precise implementation briefs and non-negotiable release/outcome gates in existing Portal V2. Update existing daily agent automation to discover/evaluate/build/test protected reversible candidates and measure results, not duplicate a scheduler.
prevention: No autonomous unprotected self-modification: the actual existing writer creates only a protected PR with Required, CodeQL, exact Netlify/Edge production readback and rollback.
Technology claims are scored against actual representative champion/challenger evals: quality, task completeness, safety, latency, cost and customer outcomes, with abstention under missing evidence.
Source observation gap prompts safe measurement repair, not conversion=0 proof, fabricated orders or upgrade promises.
Customer portal innovation is tenant-scoped, consented, accessible, privacy-preserving, and must improve actual activation, task completion, customer business value or retention, not visual novelty.
No second scheduler, publisher, egress channel, Shadow CRM, payment route, or independent Brain.

Every material change writes same fingerprint, exact code SHA, owner, signed source, experiment, actual effect, regression test and applied next natural run in existing ONE BRAIN; failed experiment preserves champion.

Agent may research and invent independently, but external permission, paid spend, credentials, security weakening, irreversible deletion, outreach consent and legal/financial commitments are hard boundaries.
